rationale: Round 0 built and ran correctly, so this candidate raises obfuscation pressure across the board while keeping tolerance for runtime and size costs moderate: the target is a tiny (1KB, 3-function) hot floating-point matmul kernel where static analysis of the multiply-accumulate chain is the main reverse-engineering vector, so control-flow passes (BCF, FLA, IBR) and arithmetic SUB get the highest security/diversity weights to obscure dataflow through the 4x4 wrap_mul4 loop; SPLIT is cheap and low-risk and complements FLA by creating flattenable blocks; IGV is enabled at moderate weight for its data-locality masking with low correctness risk; ICALL stays low because this program is nearly call-free (only main/_start/wrap_mul4), giving it little leverage while adding indirect-call overhead in a hot loop; correctness-risk weights are kept below 0.35 for the aggressive passes since the prior round confirmed the pipeline is stable, but not raised further to avoid destabilizing FP-heavy code where bogus-predicate and flattening transforms interact with tight loops.
